subject: Clarifying which hosting variants are included in the penetration test artifacts
messages:
From: Jordan Pike <jpike@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@security-consultant.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test artifacts — which hosting variants are covered?

Marcus —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. As part of our vendor assessment we need the most recent penetration test report and a clear statement of what hosting variants were included in that test (hosted API, Dedicated/reserved pools, Private/VPC, on-prem). Our auditor is particular about scope: they want to know whether attack surface testing included customer-managed endpoints (Dedicated control plane, customer VPCs) or only Redwood-managed infrastructure.

Can you confirm:
- Which hosting variants are explicitly in-scope for the attached pen test summary?
- Which components were explicitly out-of-scope (customer-managed networking, third-party clouds, customer self-hosted infra)?
- Any open remediation items that might affect our risk acceptance?

We'd like this by EOD Friday to include in the SIG questionnaire submission. If there's a short coverage matrix or diagram that makes it easy for the auditor, that would help a lot.

Thanks,
Jordan Pike
Sr. Security Engineer
Acme Corp

[Attachment: acme_questionnaire_v2.docx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pike <jpike@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts — which hosting variants are covered?

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for laying that out — good questions. Short answer up-front: the 2028 external penetration test covered Redwood-managed control plane and data plane components for the Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated pools. It did NOT include customer-managed on-prem installations or customer VPCs that host our Private deployment edge connectors.

Key clarifications:
- Hosted (Redwood API): in scope — full external pen test against public endpoints, auth flows, and backend services.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): in scope for Redwood-managed infrastructure (control plane and GPU hosts we operate). Customer-managed ingress (if customers inject their own network appliances) is out of scope.
- Private / VPC: the private control plane we run (when deployed into customer VPC via our managed connector) was partially in scope — specifically the code-paths and the connector agent we maintain. Customer-managed VPC network configuration, customer databases, and on-prem hardware remained out of scope.
- On-prem: out of scope unless Redwood delivered and operated the appliance as part of a managed on-prem engagement; standard customer-run on-prem setups were out.

I'll attach a coverage matrix and a simplified network diagram for the auditor. Laura and Monica are looping in more granular evidence (scan reports, remediation tracker).

If the auditor needs explicit language about "customer responsibility boundaries" we can provide a one-page statement highlighting responsibilities for network controls, patching, and key management in each hosting variant.

Action requested: Jordan, please confirm whether Acme considers the Private connector agent to be "customer-managed" (you said earlier that Acme plans to run the agent inside their VPC but have Redwood push updates). If so, that will influence whether we need to produce additional evidence around agent hardening.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood_pen_test_2028_summary.pdf, hosting_coverage_matrix.xlsx]

From: Jordan Pike <jpike@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@security-consultant.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts — which hosting variants are covered?

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick clarification and the matrix — that already helps. For our deployment: we'll host the connector agent inside our VPC but Redwood will manage agent upgrades via a control channel you provide. So it's a hybrid responsibility.

Two follow ups from the auditor's checklist:
1) Can you confirm whether the pen test included attempts to pivot from the connector agent into the Redwood control plane?
2) Is there a list of open findings from the pen test and estimated remediation completion dates?

If easier, feel free to push a short statement we can paste into the SIG questionnaire under "scope and responsibilities".

Appreciate it —
Jordan
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pike <jpike@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@security-consultant.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 15:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts — which hosting variants are covered?

Jordan —

Following up with the specifics you requested. See the attached hosting_coverage_matrix.xlsx (tabbed per hosting variant) and network_diagram_vpc.png. Short answers below:

1) Pivot testing: The external engagement included targeted pivot attempts from the connector agent to Redwood-managed control plane endpoints we operate. Results and mitigations are summarized in redwood_pen_test_2028_summary.pdf; none of the pivot attempts resulted in authenticated control-plane compromise.

2) Open findings: we have three medium-priority items (listed in the remediation tracker in the spreadsheet):
   - M-01: API rate-limit hardening (scheduled completion: 2028-07-25)
   - M-02: Connector agent TLS renegotiation mitigation (scheduled completion: 2028-07-31)
   - M-03: Log redaction for developer debug endpoints (scheduled completion: 2028-08-07)

We will provide a one-paragraph scope statement you can paste into the SIG/CAIQ. Draft below — feel free to use: 

"Redwood Inference's 2028 external penetration test covered Redwood-operated components for Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated environments. The test included the connector agent code paths we maintain and pivot testing to Redwood-managed control plane components. Customer-managed VPC configuration, customer-owned databases, and on-prem hardware were explicitly out of scope unless Redwood delivered and operates the appliance as noted in the contract. Customers retaining control of agent hosting are responsible for network firewall rules, patching of host OS, and local secret management. Redwood provides recommended hardening guidance and will supply targeted evidence for connector agent updates when requested."

I'll send the final signed pen test summary and remediation tracker to the Drive link and add JIRA SEC-4827 for tracking items that affect customer assessments.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: hosting_coverage_matrix.xlsx, network_diagram_vpc.png]
